key_insight: The paper shows how to efficiently learn the Slater determinant that best approximates an arbitrary fermionic many-body state, with provable guarantees on fidelity and optimization behavior.
engineering_relevance: This gives quantum engineers a principled way to compress and interpret fermionic states, supporting Hartree-Fock-style initialization, tomography, and analysis of strongly correlated systems.
method: Designs classical and quantum algorithms to search for the closest Slater determinant.
Proves the returned determinant is within ε of the optimal fidelity in time m^poly(n,1/ε).
Uses quantum copies to achieve poly(m,n,1/ε) sample complexity and analyzes the landscape around the 2/3 fidelity threshold.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical guarantees, matching hardness lower bounds under standard complexity assumptions, and an application extracting closest Slater determinants from Fermi-Hubbard neural quantum state solutions.
watch_item: The strongest guarantees are complexity-theoretic and landscape-based, so practical performance may still depend on system size, noise, and the quality of state-preparation or copy access.
